Kalpasūtra(kappasutta)
Jain. in three sections: (1) Jinacarita, ‘the biographies of the four Jinas’, especially of Mahāvīra, (2) Sthavirāvali (Therāvali), a list of Jaina schools, their branches an. their heads, (3) Sāmācārī, ‘rules for the ascetics’ especially for the rainy season (Pajjosaṇā) an. hence called Paryuṣaṇākalpa; this third part probably the oldest part of the text an. attributable to Bhadrabāhu; it forms the 8th section of Daśāśrutaskandhasūtra; the first two sections held to be additions by Devardhi; in its present form, assigned to 454 A. D., during the reign of Dhruvasena of Gujarat. On the composite authorship of the whole text an. its parts, see H. Jacobi, edn. of the Text, Leipzig, 1879, Intro. p.. 22-3; see also B. C. Law, Some Jaina Canonical Sūtras, p. 96; Wint. [Page241-b] HIL. II. p.. 461-4; Kapadia, Canonical Lit. of the Jainas, p.. 143-6; also known a. ‘Bār sem’ or ‘Bārasā’ sūtra, ‘the sūtra of 12 hundreds’, since it contains 1216 Granthas. See also Weber, Ind.
(1880), p. 755; B. M. Barua, Calcutta Review,
